subject: Re: Production impact after V4alpha + new qprofile rollout
messages:
From: Lisa Grant <lisa.grant@harborbank.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 8 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Regression: production latency + incoherent outputs after v4alpha + qprofile deploy

Sergio —

We pushed the V4alpha model with the new qprofile you recommended at 03:00 UTC this morning. Within the first hour we saw p95 latency climb from ~380ms to ~1.1s and p99 to ~1.8s. Concurrently, automated QA checks started flagging a ~5% increase in hallucination-like responses on our fraud-detection prompts (examples attached).

We have attached a small sample of production requests and a short log excerpt for your team to triage: harbor_sample_requests.json, server_logs_excerpt.txt. Traffic is still flowing but the operations team is increasingly uncomfortable. This is customer-facing and affecting our peak-hour authorization flow.

Please advise immediate next steps. If a rollback to the previous model variant is straightforward we strongly prefer that — we need stability for the next 36 hours while we evaluate.

Thanks,
Lisa Grant
Product Manager — Risk & Auth
HarborBank

--
Attachments: harbor_sample_requests.json, server_logs_excerpt.txt

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Regression: production latency + incoherent outputs after v4alpha + qprofile deploy

Lisa —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the sample artifacts. I understand the severity. I'm looping in Marissa (account) and Stephanie (eng lead) plus Vanessa from TAM.

Initial ask from our side: could you confirm whether you've already put a traffic hold or paused any critical routes? Also please confirm the top-3 request IDs from the sample that show hallucinations so we can correlate traces.

We will triage immediately; if we confirm the qprofile path is the culprit we can execute a rollback to the previous quantization profile and model variant. Stephanie — could you run the analysis and prepare rollback steps we can execute with HarborBank ops?

I will set up a short bridge if needed.

Sergio Alvarez
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Team —

This needs exec visibility. HarborBank is a strategic account (see HB-2025-RED-43) and they are reporting both latency regressions and quality regressions on fraud prompts during peak traffic. If left unresolved this risks churn and an SLA breach.

Proposed immediate plan:
- 08:30 UTC: confirm hold on non-essential routes (Harbor to confirm).
- 08:45 UTC: engineering runs targeted traces and attempts rollback to previous qprofile variant on a single AZ (canary).
- 09:15 UTC: verify p95/p99 and sample prompts for coherence improvements.
- 09:30 UTC: if canary stable, full rollback and post-mortem to follow.

Stephanie — please confirm rollback time estimate and whether the rollback requires any infra changes or elevated permissions. Vanessa — please coordinate a customer call for 08:50 UTC.

I will notify Sales leadership and request a standby for any credit/contract requests. Vivek — we may need a quick sign-off to authorize an emergency rollback and waive the 72-hour change window in their Dedicated config.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:25:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Regression: production latency + incoherent outputs after v4alpha + qprofile deploy

Quick technical summary: initial trace correlation suggests the new qprofile triggers a different kernel path and increases synchronous memory copies for long-context fraud prompts. That explains the p99 latency jump. The hallucination spike is plausibly due to a subtle numeric rounding change in the quantized GEMM path for a few token patterns; we are reproducing locally against the provided samples.

Rollback plan (canary-first):
1) Deploy previous qprofile and model variant to canary AZ (1 host) — estimated time 12-18 minutes.
2) Run targeted synthetic checks and replay the three flagged request IDs from the sample.
3) If latency/prompt coherence returns to baseline, promote rollback across fleet (additional 20-30 minutes).
4) Post-mortem and root-cause (including qprofile regressions) to follow; do not reintroduce this qprofile to HarborBank until signed-off by QA.

I've attached a short rollback_playbook.md and rollback_script.sh to this thread. We estimate full fleet rollback in ~45 minutes from start if canary passes.

One ask: we may need an expedited permission from infra/ops to override the 72-hour change lock on their Dedicated profile. Marissa / Sergio — please route to the appropriate approver.

Stephanie Nguyen
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback_playbook.md, rollback_script.sh

Subject: Emergency approval request: HarborBank rollback and 72-hour waiver

Vivek —

HarborBank (HB-2025-RED-43) is experiencing significant p99 latency regression and a measurable increase in incoherent outputs after our V4alpha + qprofile rollout. We have a canary-first rollback plan from Stephanie that should restore baseline performance in ~45 minutes pending approval to override the 72-hour Dedicated change lock.

Given the strategic importance and the SLA exposure, I recommend we approve the emergency rollback and waive the 72-hour lock for this target. We will run the standard post-mortem and produce a timeline for revalidation before any future qprofile re-introduction.

Please reply with an explicit approval so we can start the canary.

Sergio Alvarez
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
